next_step: Finalize connector SLA & begin 1M-vector POC ingest
notes:
Summary: Enterprise search vendor building RAG-enabled product for mid-large customers. Focus: embeddings + reranking, cost-per-query tight.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2025-11-12: Kickoff (FF id ff_20251112_ember_kickoff) w/ Jordan, Priya, infra. High-level arch reviewed.
- 2025-11-13: Security questionnaire submitted (SCA + SOC2 scoping).
- 2025-11-14: Architecture deep-dive: hybrid retrieval (BM25 -> ANN) + cross-encoder rerank.
- 2025-11-18: Demo of Redwood hosted latency profiles; agreed to baseline SLA targets.
- Next: start 1M-vector POC ingest; schedule connector acceptance tests.

POC & scale requirements:
- Initial ingest target: 1M vectors (POC). Production target: 300M-3B vectors within 18 months.
- Ingestion throughput: steady-state 5k upserts/day, occasional bursts 50k/day during reindex/backfill.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile at or below 200ms for end-to-end search+rerank (90k token budget per query not expected).
- Reranking: want cheap ANN candidate recall + selective cross-encoder rerank on top-10. Prefer server-side rerank with option to offload to dedicated GPUs.
- Cost target: <$0.01 per user query (aggressive); product team expecting Redwood Optimize suggestions to reduce token/rerank costs.

Vector DB / connector requirements (explicit asks):
- Support for multiple vector stores via a connector abstraction: Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Elastic. Need parity of features across connectors.
- Streaming upserts with ordered checkpoints and resume-on-failure (highly visible to infra team).
- Backfill tooling: bulk ingest with sharding controls, parallel workers, idempotent retries.
- Hybrid search: ability to combine BM25 filters and embedding ANN scorers in one query pipeline.
- Per-namespace/tenant index isolation and tenant-level replication/residency.
- Cross-encoder hook: ability to call Redwood reranker with candidate vectors and return ranked ids within 150ms P99 for top-10.
- Vector metadata filtering and composite sort (timestamp, recency, boost factors).
- Metrics and observability: per-index QPS, latencies, cache hit/miss, cardinality, vector dims. Expose to Redwood Console.

Technical preferences / constraints:
- Embedding models: prefer 1536-4096 dims; flexible to switch models. Need support for concurrent model variants and routing by workload.
- Storage: want optional encryption-at-rest with customer KMS keys.
- Network: VPC peering + dedicated private link desired for POC -> production.
- Data residency: default NA, EU for EMEA customers.

Decisions & comments from stakeholders:
- CTO (Ava Chen): "We cannot accept connector that loses ordering on upserts — must be resumable and deterministic."
- Head of Search (Marco Ruiz): leaning toward pgvector for cost but needs cross-encoder latency tests; Pinecone attractive for managed scaling but pricier.
- Infra lead wants batching advice: Redwood Optimize should recommend batch sizes and caching TTLs per workload.

Open questions / blockers:
- Security review: CISO questions around audit log retention and HSM/KMS integration unresolved.
- Connector SLA: need documented RTO/RPO for connector failures; who fixes vector drift?
- Budget: procurement needs formal pricing for 1M -> 300M ramp.

POC success criteria (explicit):
- Ingest 1M vectors within 24 hours (bulk+stream hybrid).
- End-to-end query P95 <200ms for 90% of queries during 100 qps sustained load.
- Recall@100 >= 0.85 for embedding candidate retrieval; top-10 rerank quality judged by product team manual eval set.
- Clear roadmap for growth to 300M vectors with cost-per-query projection.

Immediate next steps (owner tags):
- Jordan: finalize connector SLA doc and deliver to procurement (due 2025-11-25).
- Priya (SE): run cross-encoder rerank latency tests against pgvector & Pinecone adapters (due 2025-11-28).
- Omar (CSM): chase security Qs and provide initial SOC2 matrix.

Quick shorthands from calls: 
- "Need deterministic upserts + resume" – infra repeated 3x.
- "Cost/rerank tradeoff is dealbreaker if > $0.02/q" – product.
- "Prefer VPC peering; no public internet for PII flows."
